key_insight: This paper learns a single comorbidity score from diagnosis codes that is optimized to predict multiple clinical outcomes at once, instead of relying on fixed rule-based indices.
clinical_relevance: A learned comorbidity index could improve patient risk stratification and adjustment across outcomes beyond mortality, supporting more tailored clinical research and analytics.
method: Maps diagnosis codes to one scalar comorbidity score.
Optimizes normalized Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (nHSIC) to maximize dependence between the score and multiple outcomes.
Uses theory to identify when a unified admission-level ordering can be informative across different outcomes.
evidence_signal: In benchmark EHR datasets, the proposed MLCI outperformed strong baseline comorbidity indices across multiple evaluation metrics.
watch_item: As a learned, outcome-driven index, performance may depend on the training datasets and selected outcomes, so external validation is important before broad deployment.
